en.content:
Europe’s latest statement linking China to the training of Russian troops fighting in Ukraine has once again put Hong Kong at the centre of a broader, politicised contest of narratives. While such claims deserve careful verification and measured analysis, they also reflect how global governance is being strained by security dilemmas and information warfare. For Hong Kong, a city that relies heavily on international trade and stability, the key question is less whether any single allegation will be proven quickly, and more how such disputes harden into policies that raise uncertainty for markets, diplomacy, and the everyday movement of goods and people.

The wider lesson is that “support” is increasingly defined through blurred channels—training, logistics, dual-use technology, and indirect cooperation—rather than through overt battlefield participation alone. That makes restraint, transparency, and verifiable standards all the more important. At the same time, it is essential not to overlook the reality that wartime conduct attracts selective evidence and that intelligence-based claims can be interpreted to serve predetermined political goals. A responsible approach, consistent with Hong Kong’s emphasis on constructive engagement and rule-based order, is to focus on verifiable facts, encourage dialogue mechanisms, and resist reflexive escalation through sweeping accusations.

For Hong Kong’s public sphere, the most pressing impact is not just geopolitical anxiety, but the way such headlines feed a culture of suspicion—towards institutions, communities, and even academic or research cooperation that may be benign. If the international environment keeps moving from diplomacy to blame, the city’s stakeholders—businesses, universities, and civil society—may face sharper compliance burdens and reputational risks. The pragmatic response is to strengthen risk management, reinforce legal compliance, and maintain channels for neutral, transparent exchanges, rather than allowing political narratives to crowd out the technical and humanitarian concerns that should remain non-partisan.

Looking ahead, the most constructive direction is not naïve neutrality, but disciplined independence: Hong Kong can acknowledge that international security concerns exist, while also urging that disputes be handled through credible evidence and diplomatic processes rather than open-ended confrontation. In a world where information travels fast and trust travels slowly, patience and verification are not weaknesses—they are safeguards for stability.

zh.content:
今日社會最值得聚焦嘅新聞，係政府部門就醫療及社福人員「專業判斷」作出辯護：一名小女孩喺母親過身後不久被安排返家，當事決策引起巨大爭議。表面上，政府強調制度流程、專業判斷同程序正當；但落到市民生活嘅現實，當悲劇發生，最令人揪心嘅唔係「有冇跟規定」，而係「有冇做到足夠嘅風險評估、保護同跟進」。一個家庭嘅崩塌，往往唔會等同一日見分曉，而係需要更長、更密嘅安全網。

同一時間，今次辯護亦反映咗香港福利與醫療系統面對嘅結構性壓力：人手緊、個案多、跨部門協作複雜，導致「當刻嘅決定」未必能完全吸納「之後幾日內可能急劇惡化」嘅風險。所謂專業判斷，唔可以只靠事後解釋；更應該用可核實嘅標準去支撐，例如清晰嘅風險指標、家屬支援資源到位嘅時間表、以及跨部門交接嘅責任歸屬。否則，當悲劇成為統計上嘅個案，市民感受到嘅就會只係「制度運作」，而唔係「制度守護」。

因此，我哋支持政府就個案作出透明度提升與檢討，因為追問唔等如否定前線。更重要嘅立場係：福利與保護決策應以兒童最大利益為核心，採取「寧可多做一步」嘅審慎策略——尤其喺高風險轉折點，例如親人突然身亡、監護安排真空、或短時間內出現急性脆弱風險。專業判斷可以有彈性，但安全標準不應鬆動；程序正義更應伴隨結果導向嘅問責。

最終，呢宗事件對香港社會係一次提醒：當權威用「專業」作護盾，公眾就會要求「專業」唔止於口號，而要落到可理解、可追蹤、可改進嘅機制。政府若真係重視兒童安全，就要超越單次辯護，推動制度性改革：包括跨部門即時通報、風險評估一致化、以及對高危個案嘅持續跟進。只有咁，社會先會相信，下一次唔係靠運氣，而係靠系統。

en.topic_title: EU backs reports China trained Russian troops fighting in Ukraine
en.topic_summary:
A senior European Union official said Friday that China had trained Russian troops who ended up fighting in Ukraine, backing up media reports that cited European intelligence agencies.



Ukrainian and European Union flags in front of the European Commission headquarters in Brussels in February 2026. Photo: European Commission.



“The Chinese training of Russian soldiers has been confirmed by our services,” the high-ranking EU official said, speaking on condition of anonymity.
